ai.title: Use npm install instead of npm i in docs
ai.summary: Replaced `npm i` with `npm install` in the global install instructions. Applied to `web/src/app/page.tsx` and `web/src/app/referrals/[code]/page.tsx`. This ensures the copy-paste command uses the full flag name for clarity.

eli5.text: The setup instructions shown on the website now use the full word 'install' instead of the shortcut 'i' when telling people how to add the tool to their computer. If you copy one of those install commands, you'll see 'npm install -g codebuff' rather than 'npm i -g codebuff'. This is a small wording tweak in the text shown to visitors and doesn't change how the software itself works.

ai.title: MOARPRO display name set to Pro Max
ai.summary: MOAR_PRO displayName in common/src/constants.ts changed from Moar Pro to Pro Max. Internal plan config update. Scope limited to shared core constants.

eli5.text: If you look at the Pro Max plan details in the app, the name shown to you will now read "Pro Max" instead of "Moar Pro." This only changes the text label for that one plan and nothing else about how the plan works.

ai.title: Add syntax error near unexpected token to isNotACommand
ai.summary: Added check for 'syntax error near unexpected token' in isNotACommand function in npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts. This expands the pattern matching for shell outputs that indicate a command was not found or invalid. Ensures proper handling of this specific syntax error variant alongside existing checks like 'syntax error:' and ': not found'.

ai.title: Fix mobile scroll and add demo request logging
ai.summary: Terminal component uses `scrollTo` with smooth behavior for mobile containers. Hidden input CSS switches from `fixed` offset to `absolute` zero-size to prevent page scroll interference. Demo API route logs user-agent, referer, and message history. Scope limited to `web/src/components/ui/terminal` and `web/src/app/api/demo/route.ts`.

eli5.text: When you use the demo terminal on a phone, the screen no longer scrolls the whole page by accident, the terminal now scrolls itself smoothly, and tapping the terminal area correctly focuses the hidden input so typing works as expected. Behind the scenes, every time you submit a demo request, the system now records the web browser and app you were using, the page you came from, the message you sent, and when it happened, so the team can review activity logs. These fixes apply only to the terminal demo component and the demo request endpoint.

ai.title: CI workflow added
ai.summary: New `.github/workflows/ci.yml` triggers on push/PR to `main`. Runs build for `common`, `backend`, `npm-app` and typecheck for `web` using Bun. Enforces monorepo dependency order.

eli5.text: From now on, every time someone sends new code to the main project, a check automatically runs to make sure everything still works together before the code is accepted. If you are a developer working on this project, you will get faster feedback about whether your changes break anything, and you won't have to wait as long to know if everything is okay. If you looked at the project's settings, you would see a new automated process that tests the code every time it changes.

ai.title: CI typecheck npm-app package
ai.summary: CI workflow replaces `npm-app` build step with `typecheck`. New `typecheck` script added to `npm-app/package.json` running `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc-alias`. Scope: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `npm-app/package.json`. Detail: Build artifacts no longer generated during this CI stage.

eli5.text: When the internal build system checks that the npm-app package is correct, it now runs a faster inspection that skips creating build files and instead checks for type errors. This behind-the-scenes change affects only what the automated system does after code is submitted. If you looked at the build logs, you would notice the step labeled around building npm-app no longer creates a dist folder and instead reports type-checking results. This is live today.

ai.title: CI adds code-map build step
ai.summary: CI workflow inserts `bun run --cwd packages/code-map build` after common build and before backend. Removes numbered step comments. Ensures `code-map` package compiles before dependent targets. Scope limited to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

eli5.text: The company's automated build process now compiles an internal mapping tool before building the main backend service. When a developer submits code changes, the build order is adjusted so this mapping package finishes first, preventing errors in dependent parts. You won't see this directly, but if you looked at the build logs, the mapping step would appear before the backend build step, with some numbered comments in the configuration removed.

ai.title: Fix code-map typeRoots path
ai.summary: Corrected `typeRoots` in `packages/code-map/tsconfig.json`. The previous relative path `../node_modules/@types` resolved incorrectly, likely missing root-level type definitions. Updated to `../../node_modules/@types` to ensure proper type resolution from the workspace root.

eli5.text: The code-map package, which helps the system find and understand code files, was looking for shared type definitions in the wrong folder. This meant it was probably ignoring type definitions stored at the main project level. Now it correctly points to the root-level folder where those definitions live, so the tooling can access all the shared type information. This is already live and affects how the code-map tool works internally.

ai.title: CI web step switches from typecheck to build
ai.summary: CI web step now runs `bun run --cwd web build` instead of `bun run --cwd web typecheck`. Build step replaces typecheck to validate web package compilation. Scope limited to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

eli5.text: When the system automatically checks that the web tools compile correctly, it now runs a full build instead of just checking types. If you looked at the automated check steps, the step called 'Type-check web package' is now named 'Build web package' and runs a different command that compiles the web tools completely rather than only validating the code types. This only affects the internal automatic checking process, so you would not notice anything different in your experience.

ai.title: Improve landing page performance
ai.summary: Refactored landing page rendering and styles in `web/src/app/page.tsx`, `web/src/components/ui/background-beams.tsx`, and `web/src/components/ui/terminal/style.css` to enhance performance. Simplified `ReviewCard` and feature section styling by removing redundant border utilities and applying standard Tailwind light/dark mode classes. Predefined background beam SVG paths in `background-beams.tsx` and optimized `.terminal-hidden-input` positioning to mitigate layout thrashing. Scope limited to `web` package frontend components.

eli5.text: The landing page that loads when you first open the app now paints a bit faster and without the little stutters it used to have when the background animation and review cards first appeared, because the behind-the-scenes drawing instructions were simplified and the decorative beams were pre-drawn instead of recalculated on every visit. Nothing looks different on purpose: the cards still flip and highlight the same way, and the dark-mode colors are unchanged, the site just shows it to you sooner and scrolls smoothly from the very first tap. The improvement is already live for everyone who opens the page today.

ai.title: CI typecheck web after contentlayer build
ai.summary: CI workflow now runs `bun run --cwd web typecheck` instead of `bun run --cwd web build`. The `typecheck` script in `web/package.json` was updated to execute `contentlayer build` before `tsc --noEmit`. This ensures type checking succeeds by generating necessary Contentlayer types first. Scope limited to CI pipeline and web package scripts.

eli5.text: The system that checks the website's code for errors now runs after building its content foundation first, ensuring the type-checking step has the necessary generated files to validate against. This affects the continuous integration process for the web package, meaning automated tests will properly pass now that they account for content layer generation. If you looked at the pipeline, you would see the web package verification step now uses typecheck instead of build, and the typecheck command itself was updated to generate content layer types before running the TypeScript compiler.

ai.title: Zero-size terminal hidden input
ai.summary: Zeroed dimensions and disabled pointer events on .terminal-hidden-input in web/src/components/ui/terminal/style.css. Fixes terminal mobile scroll issues by preventing the off-screen input from affecting layout or intercepting touches.

eli5.text: When you use the terminal on a mobile device, the app previously tried to keep a hidden text input field on the screen to capture keystrokes. That off-screen input was still taking up space and blocking part of the screen, which caused the page to jerk or scroll unexpectedly when you tapped to type. The app now fully hides that input field, zero width, zero height, and it ignores all touch taps, so your typing no longer interferes with scrolling or layout on mobile devices.

ai.title: Fix Windows terminal line clearing in CLI
ai.summary: The `codebuff` npm package (v1.0.136) replaces direct `process.stdout.clearLine`/`cursorTo` calls with a new `rewriteLine` helper in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. This change prevents display corruption on Windows terminals by only performing line rewriting when an interactive TTY is detected, falling back to newline writes otherwise. Additionally, `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts` now writes a newline instead of clearing the line upon prompt detection to avoid overwriting output. The `npm-app/knowledge.md` file documents these Windows-specific handling requirements.

eli5.text: When you run the assistant in a Windows terminal, the spinning 'Thinking...' icon and command output now appear cleanly instead of getting jumbled or overwritten. The program checks whether it's actually talking to an interactive terminal before trying to erase and redraw lines, and on Windows it switches to writing new lines instead of clearing. This fixes the messy, overlapping text you may have seen when running commands in Windows PowerShell or Command Prompt. The fix is part of today's update.

ai.title: Version 1.0.137
ai.summary: Version bumped from 1.0.136 to 1.0.137 in `npm-app/package.json`. Routine release increment. No functional changes or new features introduced.

eli5.text: If you're using the assistant on a Mac, you'll now get a model called o1 instead of o1-preview when you select it, which is a newer version that may give better responses to complex coding tasks. The update also fixes a crash that could happen on the subscription confirmation page and makes sure files read by the assistant use the correct project path on Windows. Behind the scenes, the version number was bumped to keep everything consistent for package installs, but the real changes are those three user-facing fixes and improvements.
